record.description:
The card pack rigging animation will be done using a bone system. This way, we can animate all the the card as long as their shape doesn't shape. 

Overall vibe: The players will see this animation A LOT. So the animation should be fast enough, but still appealing.

The generic flow:

![image.png]([URL_52488])

2.  for "Tap to Open" action to take place. (we're not doing the hand)

   ![image.png]([URL_52487])


3. The pack rips open. As the sides come apart the card is revealed. When the ripped card parts are out of the screen, the card becomes bigger. From there 3 scenerios can happen:

a. Displays a "new" tag if the player doesn't own the item and let players to clam.
b. Don't display the new tag if the player already owns. Players can claim.

c. The cards can turn into bones.

record.description:
Update:

It seems like reloading the design level scene and  thus reloading the level and untether the tracks from each tier, but this reloading process doesn't seem feasible or scalable.

> 
>
> @Blake there is a bug or unintended feature with the dynamic difficulty in the level editor.
>
> * You start with just default tier 0. When you create hard or easy tiers such as +1 or -1, all the monster tracks and item tracks are cloned.
> * If you change any of these monster track in, doesn't matter which difficulty tier you're editing, it CHANGES ALL.
> * This is the same for item tracks.
> * For me this is less of an issue if I am making a harder track today, because then I would just add additional monster tracks with the same timestamps but just create separate quantity. So for example I have tier 0, spawn 5 punks at 30 seconds, for the difficulty, I would just add another track that says spawn 3 punks at 30 seconds, so for a total of 8 punks at 30th second when combining both tracks.
> * This becomes a huge problem when I want to create an easier tier. Because the inherited monster tracks really needs to be dialed down, so the 5 punks at 30th second? It needs to be dialed down to 3 punks only. But I can't do that because changing it to 3 on the easier tier, will change that same track for tier 0 and 1 and all other tiers. But I can't delete this track and just create a new track with 3 punks only, because this deletes that track for all other tiers...
> * I think the solution is to make sure one you create new easy or harder tiers, the inherited tracks are not tethered to one another, I'm guessing this is a bug because in the level objects...

record.title: Define card accessibility based on collections for packs
record.description:
'@[PERSON_NAME_0054] said:

> @[PERSON_NAME_0120] Card accessibility will be based off "collections". Currently we have 3 collections.
>
> * Day 0 Collection (Basically all the items a player sees in the first 100 levels, the default "starter pack")
> * "The Deadly Ensemble" (Instruments, will not appear in first 100 levels)
> * "Circuit Slayers" (Personal electronics, will not appear in the first 100 levels)
> * Only cards that are marked as "Active" in the card data can be obtained and upgraded by the player.
> * For each "pack" we release, the pool of cards will be determined by the collection assigned to that pack, and very often it includes more than 1 collection.
> * Today we only have ONE pack. And it will have ALL THREE collection I just mentioned here.
> * However if the collection is not unlocked because the players have not reached a certain milestone, then the packs they have will only contain what they have unlocked.
> * So in the end the net pool of cards are: (Collection assigned to the pack) - (Collection not unlocked by the player) - (Cards not "active" marked by the designer)

record.title: Implement Pop-Up Offer Progression Logic
record.description:
**Description:**
We are introducing a tiered **pop-up offer system** in **Zombie Match**, consisting of three sequential packs:

1. **Day Zero Pack ($2.99)**
2. **Provisions Pack ($4.99)**
3. **Strategist's Pack ($9.99)**

These packs follow a progression logic and share the same pop-up UI behavior as implemented in **Domino Delights**.

---

### **Offer Flow Logic:**

* **Day Zero Pack**
  * **Trigger:** After player completes **Level 25**
  * **Availability:** Live for **3 days**
  * **One-time offer**
  * **Must be purchased to unlock the next offer**
* **Provisions Pack**
  * **Trigger:** Shown only **after Day Zero Pack is purchased**
  * **Availability:** Live for **4 days**
  * **One-time offer**
  * **Must be purchased to unlock the next offer**
* **Strategist’s Pack**
  * **Trigger:** Shown only **after Provisions Pack is purchased**
  * **Availability:** Live for **5 days**
  * **One-time offer**

---

### **Shared Offer Behavior:**

* Only **one offer is active at a time** per user.
* All offers appear under the **same HUD icon (top-right corner)**.
* Pop-up animation, tracking, and timer logic should reuse the **existing functionality from Domino Delights.**

---

**Notes:**

* Offers must expire cleanly if the user does not purchase within the time limit.
* If the user does not buy the Day Zero Pack, the other two offers will never appear.
* Ensure purchase status is persistently stored and respected across sessions.

This system allows us to gradually upsell players with increasing value while keeping the interface clean and non-intrusive.

record.description:
The bugs we’ve been putting off is starting to catch up to us now that we have 50 levels of solid play.

Gameplay issues:

* Level ends prematurely where as a boss spawns right as the win screen appears.

* Enrage doesn’t apply to newly spawned monsters, unless enrage happens after the monster has spawned. (Behavior should be pre-enraged)

Dynamic Difficult Design Oversight Fix
record.description:
Currently, the players advances a tier whenever they win 8 out of last 10 games.

This means by level 40, a player can easily be labeled as tier 4, which is often the case given how easy our game is early on.

However many of our levels only have 2 tiers of difficult, 0 and 1. And the idea is that if a player loses 4 in a row, they get demoted a player tier. So 4 -> 3 -> 2 and -> 1. However this creates a problem.

A player is difficulty tier 4, plays a difficulty tier 1 level, gets stuck, loses 4 in a row, they are demoted to tier 3. They still load difficulty tier 1 level, and continues to lose. A player would need to lose 12 times for them to actually get to difficulty tier 0 for that level. This defeats the whole purpose of downgrading them. Losing 12 in a row will cause a user to churn.

Solution: when a player is demoted, we also need to demote the level difficulty for the level they are currently on.

So if a player is demoted from tier 4 -> 3, and they were playing tier 1 difficulty and failed, that level will load the tier 0 version.

The following level, it will just go back to normal, meaning if a tier 3 level is available, that's the level that will load for the player. Otherwise we load the tier difficulty closes to the player's current tier.

record.title: Reward Box 2D Opening Animation
record.description:
![image.png]([URL_52355])

Figma Link: [https://www.figma.com/design/TvRw8na5iGd3NynbSRUGFy/Zombie-Match-3D?node-id=782-2&p=f&t=VRKdThpBQWvZBKD4-0](https://www.figma.com/design/TvRw8na5iGd3NynbSRUGFy/Zombie-Match-3D?node-id=782-2&p=f&t=VRKdThpBQWvZBKD4-0)


We need a **short, snappy 2D animation** for the Weekly Contest reward screen. The animation should bring the purple reward chest to life in a way that feels satisfying and rewarding, but **fast-paced and skippable**. 

The animation leads into the **reward icon reveal** (handled separately in development). So, we need to account for that when deciding the timing of the box opening animation. 

Guidelines:

* You can decide the animation direction. Both opening up and sliding to the side are acceptable. But I think a small wobble followed by a generic opening upward is the most satisfying. 
* Animation should be **no longer than 0.5-1 second,** since we need to spare time for the icon reveal, as well. The whole scene should take more than 2 seconds. 
* Motion should be **clean and sharp**— let's avoid floaty easing or long anticipation.
* This part of the animation should support being **interruptible** without breaking the icon reveal and claim flow, **just in case** we decide to add a skipping /freezing later.
  without breaking the claim flow.
* Please use **simple VFX flourishes** as needed (light burst, sparkles), but keep it aligned with our current visual style.

record.title: Teams' missing Screen - Out of lives
record.description:

record.title: Track Player Card Inventory and Sync to BigQuery
record.description:
### **Requirements:**

#### **1. Inventory Data Capture on Player Login to the backend:**

* When a player logs into the backend, capture and send the following for each card:
  * `player_id`
  * `card_id` (integer)
  * `card_level`
    * `0` = Not owned / Locked
    * `1-5` = Owned, corresponds to card level
  * `timestamp` of the login

#### **2. BigQuery Sync:**

* Send this card inventory data to **BigQuery once per day**, ideally on first login of the day.
* Each row in the table should represent a unique player–card inventory.

#### **3. Lookup Table for Card Metadata:**

* Create a **separate BigQuery table** mapping `card_id` → `card_name` (or human-readable identifier).

---

### **Data Schema:**

**Player Card Inventory Table (card_inventory):**

`player_id (string) card_id (int) card_level (int) timestamp (datetime)`

**Card Metadata Table (card_metadata) :**

`card_id (int) card_name (string)`

This will allow us to query and segment players by card ownership and progression, and support future features such as dynamic offers, A/B tests, and balancing decisions.

record.title: Dynamic Difficulty
record.description:
# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Monster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with

Punk A | Punk B

Punk B | Punk C

Punk C | Punk D

Punk D | Brute A

Boss 1 | Boss 3

Boss 2 | Boss 4

Boss 10 | Boss 10

If the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.

The other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster "rank" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the "next rank" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:
Punk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C

Then Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.

This will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. This will also prevent us from overcrowding the level with simply too many monsters.

record.title: Reorganize Event Icon Grouping and Replacement
record.description:
**Description:**
Currently, we have many event icons displayed on the main screen. To improve clarity and user navigation, we can adopt a grouping approach similar to *Royal Match*.

**Proposed Change:**

* Group **only-reward events** (e.g., Zombie Lane, Season Pass, Quests) on one side (e.g., right).
* Keep **playable events** on the opposite side (e.g., left).
* Alternatively, we can switch sides — placement order is flexible as long as the grouping remains consistent.

**Goal:**
Improve UI organization and help players quickly identify different event types.

![image.png]([URL_52778])

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* Event icons are consistently grouped by type.
* UI remains balanced and visually clear.
* No loss of functionality or discoverability for any event.
* The order of them is consistent when another event icon is not visible. 

**Adjustable Parameters:**

Since we need to test how it looks in the game. We need certain adjustable parameters for next iterations. 

* The group of an event
* The interchangeable placement for different groups (we can make right icons in the left for later)
* The order of an event within its group

record.title: Add Blunder Count by Level to Analytics
record.description:
**Description:**
We forgot to capture a key gameplay metric in our analytics: the number of **blunders** per level—specifically, how often players **fill up their match platform and lose** due to unforced errors, not monster attacks.

This will help us better understand the true cause of level failures. Some losses currently attributed to monster damage may actually be due to player mistakes.

**Why it matters:**

* Allows us to distinguish between unforced errors and system-driven defeats
* Helps with level balancing and difficulty tuning
* Improves accuracy of failure reason attribution

**Action Items:**

* Track and log **blunder count** per player per level
* Include it in the existing analytics pipeline
* Add this metric to relevant dashboards (e.g., Level Performance or Failure Breakdown)

record.title: Difficulty Scaling Through Algo
record.description:
We are scaling difficulty with player's tier level and the actual level they are on.

Here is the 1st part based on the level they are within the game.

Level 1-50 = 0% bonus to monster HP

Level 51-100 = 5% bonus to monster HP

Level 101-150 = 10% bonus to monster HP

Every 50 levels from here on out = 5% more.

Here is the 2nd part on scaling monster HP based on player's tier. Each player starts at tier 0 when they first enter the game, but can move up and down tiers based on their win/loss record.

For each tier beyond 0, assign a 3% bonus to monster HP, so tier 4 = 12% bonus.

I believe tier 1 can be reached as early as level 11. And after that the fastest way to level up is win 8 out of 10 games. So by level 51, the highest tier a player can reach is tier 6.

record.title: Create Test Levels For Object Composition
record.description:
We want to test the current resize on tap area logic. 

1. Creating a range of Unity primitives based on tap real estate on the board
   (Baseline range)
2. Levels where primitives and resembling objects are side by side 
   (Perceptual consistency evaluation)
3. Levels with multiple primitives and multiple resembling objects side by side. 
   (Real-world scaling composition evaluation)
   
   
   Branch Active: [PERSON_NAME_0019]/itemcompositiontest
   
   Task 1: Decide Min-Max Threshold 
   
   We need to decide what's the smallest and largest tap area we allow players on an object from a difficulty and aesthetics standpoint. 
   
   a. Minimum First 
   
   The minimum tap area should be visible on the screen. If levels are made out of the smallest tap area objects, it shouldn't look absurd. And it should still be clickable comfortably. 
   
   b. Maximum Second
   
   The max is more straightforward. It shouldn't be big enough that the object looks too out of place especially compared to the decided small item. Think sheriff bagde vs couch. 
   
   To help decide, these are the test levels (unchecked for prod)
   
   1. CylinderMinTapArea
   
   Shows beer mugs (bulky cylinder) with 0.2, 0.25, 0.3, and 0.35 script sizing. 
   
   2. BadgeMinTapArea
   
    Show badges (flat small) with 0.25, 0.275, and 0.3 script sizing. 

      3\. RakeMinTapArea

      Rakes in different colors, 0.5,0.6, and 0.7 in script sizing. 

      4\. BeerMaxTap
      
 Beers in different sizes 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 in script sizing and a 0.3 beer mug for comparison    and perceptual consistency.

5. CouchMaxTap
   
   This is the bulkiest object so it's the ultimate threshold for maximum tap area. This level has couch script sizes 0.75, 0.85, and 0.95 and a 0.3 beer mug for comparison.

Task 2: Decide shape categories (prefab sizing among peers)

Every item gets a shape label according to these categories 

1. Narrow Vertical (fork, pen, wine bottle, billiard stick)
2. Flat (chocolate, plate, pizza box, badge, music note, letters)
3. Bulky Polygon (gift box, washing machine, barrel)
4. Bulky Wide (couch, fridge, bicycle)
5. Tall Irregular (lamp, plunger)


Task 3: Define global min and max for each shape

1. For example the smallest narrow vertical item we will have in the game is a "rake"
2. The smallest flat item we will have in the game is "badge"

Task 4: Resize things accordingly.

Don't over adjust

record.title: Zombie Gamemode #1 Spec (Operation: No Exit) "Endless Mode"
record.description:
We are going to add an "Endless Mode" as the first game mode of Zombie Match 3D. Working title is Operation: No Exit. 

Alternate names: Forever Brains, Till Death Loops Us Apart, Last Zom Standing, Match ‘Em Dead

There isn't a lot of art need for this one, just simple pre-level dialogue UIs and perhaps a few differentiators for the level. 

Some brain storm jump points. 

Mechanic #1 Item Dump 

If we want to make the endless mode more about matching, we can go an item dump to the board in fixed intervals. That way, there is a clear fail condition to end the endless of the endless mode and players can be scored based on how long they survived. If the board gets full beyond allowed capacity, we fail. Extra hard if each item dump has different items. 

Pros: Perfect for the match-oriented players. 
Cons: Can get frustrating very quickly. 

Mechanic #2 Zombie Difficulty

If we want to focus on zombie killing aspect to engage the players, we can opt for giving players ammunition of the same item set and weapon items to make them carrots on the otherwise repetitive mode. The zombie waves get progressively harder and if they reach the cannon; it's game over. 

Pros: Has flow, momentum, and possibility to help players zone out with repetitive action. 
Cons: If the player is more of a "matcher", they won't find it challenging enough because zombies won't do much for them.
